name: Structure

subjectOf.text: Concentration produces instability and dispersion produces stability: the more concentrated a structure is, the more unstable it is, because little changes can cause major structural change, while a spread out pattern remains spread out when disturbed.
subjectOf.abstract: The more concentrated a structure is, the more unstable it is. The more spread out a pattern is, the more stable it is
subjectOf.citation: Craig Calcaterra, Wulf A. Kaal, Preface to (2021). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3782191
scope_conditions: any structure characterized by concentration or dispersion

subjectOf.text: Three validator families share a mean accuracy of 0.75 while differing in structure: one is homogeneous at 0.75, one has each validator reliable at 0.90 on two hash-drawn tags and at 0.60 on the other two so that domain-scoped reputation has something to find, and one has five validators at 0.90 and fifteen at 0.70, a competent minority.
subjectOf.abstract: Intelligence models increasingly learn from data that earlier Intelligence models produced, and when that loop repeats the rare cases disappear first. This paper preregisters a test of whether a reputation-weighted validator pool, filtering the training data of a recursive replacement loop, keeps those rare cases alive. The outcomes remain sealed until a replication of the original model-collapse result succeeds.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Can Reputation Prevent Model Collapse? A Preregistered Test of Reputation-Weighted Data Filtering (2026). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=7598518
scope_conditions: The validators are simulated and err independently given their accuracy, which depends only on the tag.
The families are a property of the design, fixed before any run.
